chapters.summary: John commends Gaius for his hospitality to traveling brethren, rebukes Diotrephes for his self-seeking, domineering ways, and urges believers to imitate what is good.
keyPoints: John commends Gaius for walking in the truth and for his eager hospitality toward traveling brethren and strangers.
He rebukes Diotrephes, who loves to have the preeminence, refuses to receive the brethren himself, and forbids others who would receive them, even casting them out of the church.
He commends Demetrius's good testimony and urges believers to imitate what is good, not what is evil.
chapters.application: In the life of the church, welcome travelers and fellow believers with love, imitate what is good, guard against pride and the desire to dominate others, and support one another in truth and love.
